match.reason: The closest bank point, Reducing inequality, covers public services as only one of four mechanisms alongside taxes, welfare and minimum wages, and its card and questions centre on those other mechanisms, so it is broader than this single idea about universal Medicare and public schools.

draft.title: Services for everyone
card: Some services are provided by governments so that everyone can use them, whatever their income. Two examples are health care and education.
Australia's public health insurance scheme. It pays all or part of the cost of many doctor visits and public hospital care for people who live in Australia and are eligible.
Government schools that teach children without charging tuition fees. Families may still pay for some costs, such as uniforms and excursions.
These services are paid for mostly from taxes. A family on a low income can see a doctor and send children to school without paying the full cost. This lifts their living standards.
draft.remember: Medicare and public schools give people on low incomes access to health care and education they might not otherwise afford.

a.q: How do Medicare and public schools help raise the living standards of people on low incomes?
opts: They give access to health care and education at low cost
They pay people a set sum of money to spend as they wish
They make sure that everyone earns the same income each year
They take a larger share of income from people who earn more
a.why: Medicare and public schools provide services, so people on low incomes can use health care and education without paying the full cost. Regular payments of money are transfer payments, which work differently.
a.clue: Think about what is provided: services, not cash.

b.q: The Nguyen family lives in Alice Springs and has a low income. A child breaks an arm and is treated at a public hospital under Medicare. The family pays little or nothing. What does this show?
opts: A service open to all can lift a low income family's living standards
The family must be getting a payment of cash from the government
Public services can only ever help people who have a low income
The family has more wealth than it would have without Medicare
b.why: Medicare lets the family get care whatever their income, so a medical emergency does not cut their living standards as much. The care is a service, not a cash payment, and the card does not say it is limited to low income families.
b.clue: Medicare is open to everyone who is eligible, whatever they earn.
